inline_text:
Following the validation examples in #36, I'd like to contribute a concrete contrast case: **interactive work with a separately approved final save**.

A user reviews and adjusts photo previews while watching a video. In Radiolaria's [Workspace test](https://github.com/AAkhtanin/hedgehog-os/blob/800f38c3407b3f4ec93dc943c977ffeecb614881/docs/showcase/radiolaria_os_v01/chapters/09_workspace.md), stopping the audio process leaves photo work intact; only the affected media branch is recomputed, and video continues silently, as permitted by the task. Recovery does not reactivate the expired pre-failure action packet.

Saving the final selection remains a separate approval boundary. A [focused test](https://github.com/AAkhtanin/hedgehog-os/blob/800f38c3407b3f4ec93dc943c977ffeecb614881/tests/test_ephemeral_workspace_v01.py#L432-L468) changes a rating after approval, rejects the old approval and accepts a newly approved result.

The Single-Agent Process with Human Approval checklist explicitly excludes co-editing and steering during execution. This case shows why that distinction matters: the final SAVE illustrates the approval pattern, while the surrounding interactive work and selective recovery need a broader composition.

**Proposed use:** a scope-comparison example for the catalogue, not a claim that the whole Workspace fits the single-agent RA. The devices are local software services; the failure run and approval interaction are scripted tests.
